Story:

Character 1
Name: Florence Niedler
Description: A nurse who works at Hertz Hospital. Has a worrying tendency to offer unnecessary treatments to everyone she meets.
Character 2
Name: Kay Faraday
Description: A mysterious young woman brought to the High Prosecutors' Offices by Florence Niedler. She appears to have lost her memory, but...
Character 3
Name: Hilda Hertz
Description: The head of Hertz Hospital. Carried out the preliminary inspection of the victim in this case.
Character 4
Name: Franziska von Karma
Description: Daughter of my mentor, Manfred von Karma. She is a highly talented prosecutor, and is currently working with Interpol.
Character 5
Name: Eustace Winner
Description: The greatest prosecutor ever to prosecute... according to himself, anyway. In actual fact, his relationship with logic is tenuous at best.
Character 6
Name: Verity Gavèlle
Description: A district court judge and member of the Committee for Prosecutorial Excellence, who also acts as its mouthpiece.
Character 7
Name: Rosie Ringer
Description: The victim in this case. She was a defense attorney, and served on the Committee alongside Judge Gavèlle.
Character 8
Name: Excelsius Winner
Description: Former chief prosecutor, current Chairman of the Committee, and Eustace Winner's father. Has a tendency to burst into tears over nothing.
Character 9
Name: Eddie Fender
Description: Senior partner at Edgeworth and Co. He's trying to get me to become a defense attorney.
Character 10
Name: Ema Skye
Description: A high school student looking to become a forensic investigator, and the younger sister of my former boss.
Character 11
Name: Lotta Hart
Description: A freelance photojournalist who I've met in the past. Known for her ability to sniff out scoops and snap them with her trusty camera.
Evidences:
Evidence 0
Name: Prosecutor's Badge
Description: Proof of my profession. However, I prefer to keep it in my pocket.
Evidence 1
Name: Yatagarasu Pin

Name: Jammin' Ninja Mask

Evidence 3
Name: Letter
Description: A letter Kay was carrying. It is addressed to her.
Evidence 4
Name: Promise Notebook
Description: A book of promises Kay made to her father when she was a little girl. What was it doing in the Committee chamber?
Evidence 5
Name: Ticket Stub
Description: Stub from a ticket granting entry to the viewing platform on top of the Bigg Building.
Evidence 6
Name: Magenta Flower
Description: A magenta flower made of fabric that is usually worn on the chest as a decoration. Also known as a corsage. A magenta flower made of fabric that is usually worn on the chest as a decoration. Torn from the victim's clothes.
Evidence 7
Name: Bigg Building Pamphlet
Description: Contains a cross-section of the building and a plan of the viewing platform. [caption] On the roof is the viewing platform. Evidence 8
Name: Kay's Recollections
Description: Kay remembers a person coming from beyond the concession stand and pushing her off of the building.

Name: Keycard
Description: A keycard that grants entry to the Committee chamber. Found in the victim's hand.
Evidence 11
Name: Autopsy Report
Description: Initial findings of Dr. Hilda Hertz. Cause of death: Stab wounds to left chest. Head injury sustained post mortem. Death occurred as a result of a heavy blow to the head with a circular object. Chest wounds inflicted post-mortem.
Evidence 12
Name: Keycard Record
Description: Record of keycards used to enter the Committee chamber.
Evidence 13
Name: Victim's Letter
Description: A letter that appears to have been written to the victim by Kay.
Evidence 14
Name: Broken Plushie
Description: The stuffed animal we originally found in the Zheng Fa presidential plane. Missing its left horn. Fitted with a recording device that captured part of a conversation. One of the people recorded had a prominent burn.
Evidence 15
Name: Masks
Description: A selection of various masks was kept on a rack. Each participant in the auction wore one.
Evidence 16
Name: Ringleader's Appearance
Description: Ringleader wore a white jacket, white gloves, a magenta flower, and a mask. Age and gender could not be discerned. Ringleader wore a white jacket, white gloves, a magenta flower, and a mask. Also had a tattoo on the part of their face the mask didn't cover.
Evidence 17

<think>
Okay, let's tackle this problem step by step. The user wants me to find a pair of evidence and testimony that contradict each other. First, I need to go through the provided evidence and testimonies to see where there might be inconsistencies.

Starting with the evidence. Let's look at Evidence 8: Kay's Recollections. It says that Kay remembers a person coming from beyond the concession stand and pushing her off the building. Then, looking at the testimonies, Testimony 3 is from Kay as well, where she mentions seeing something red under the cherry tree. 

Wait, the Bigg Building's pamphlet (Evidence 7) mentions a cherry tree on the left-most edge and a candy stand on the right. If Kay was pushed from beyond the concession stand (which is on the right), but she saw something red under the cherry tree (left), that might not directly contradict yet. But let's check other testimonies. 

Testimony 4 says someone was walking towards her from the other side of the stand. The stand is the candy stand. So if the person came from beyond the concession stand (Evidence 8) and was walking towards her from the other side (Testimony 4), maybe that's consistent. However, Testimony 3 mentions seeing something red under the cherry tree. If the person pushing her was on the opposite side of the stand (right side), but she saw something under the cherry tree (left side), maybe there's a contradiction in the direction or location. 

Wait, maybe there's another contradiction. Let's check other evidence. Evidence 6 is a magenta flower torn from the victim's clothes. The Ringleader's Appearance (Evidence 16) mentions wearing a magenta flower. If the victim had the magenta flower, but the ringleader was wearing one, maybe that's a connection. But how does that tie into the testimonies?

Looking at Testimony 3 again: "from under the cherry tree... I feel like... I saw something red." The victim was wearing a red raincoat (Evidence 22), so maybe the red thing she saw was the victim. But if the victim was pushed from the right (concession stand side), and Kay saw her under the cherry tree (left), maybe there's a spatial inconsistency. 

Alternatively, if the person pushing her was on the right side, but she saw the victim under the cherry tree (left), that could mean she was looking in a different direction when the push happened, which might not be a direct contradiction. Hmm.

Wait, Evidence 8 says the person came from beyond the concession stand (right side) and pushed her off. If she was looking at the cherry tree (left side) when she saw something red, maybe she wasn't facing the person pushing her. That might not contradict, but maybe there's another angle. 

Looking at Testimony 4: someone walking towards her from the other side of the stand. That would be the same as Evidence 8's direction. So that's consistent. But Testimony 3 mentions the cherry tree. Maybe the problem is that if she was pushed from the right (concession stand side), she wouldn't be under the cherry tree (left) when she fell. Unless the building's layout allows for movement from the stand to the cherry tree quickly. 

Alternatively, if the person pushing her was on the right, but she saw the victim under the cherry tree (left) before being pushed, that's possible. Maybe the contradiction is elsewhere. 

Wait, the autopsy report (Evidence 11) says the cause of death was a heavy blow to the head with a circular object, and chest wounds were post-mortem. The candelabrum (Evidence 9) is a three-armed candle holder found by the body. If the candelabrum was the murder weapon, but the chest wounds were post-mortem, maybe that's a contradiction. However, the question is about evidence and testimony contradicting each other, not between evidence.

Looking back at the testimonies. Testimony 3: saw something red under the cherry tree. Testimony 4: someone coming from the other side of the stand. If the red thing was the victim, but the victim was pushed from the stand side, maybe she saw the victim before being pushed. That might not contradict. 

Wait, maybe the key is in the direction. If she was pushed from the concession stand (right), but she saw something under the cherry tree (left), that implies she was facing left when the push happened. But if someone was coming from the right (concession stand), she would have to be facing right to see them. This could be a contradiction between her recollection (Evidence 8) and her testimony (Testimony 3). 

So Evidence 8 says the person came from beyond the concession stand (right), but Testimony 3 says she saw something under the cherry tree (left). If she was facing left, the person pushing her from the right wouldn't be in her line of sight. Therefore, there's a contradiction between her memory of the direction of the attacker and what she saw. That would mean Evidence 8 (Kay's Recollections) and Testimony 3 (her statement about the cherry tree) contradict each other. 

Therefore, the answer would be {"evidence": 8, "testimony": 3}.
</think>
